answer: Commit the hash, reveal inside the audit window, let an agent with no stake in the outcome check the reveal. A failed audit slashes the full receipt rather than a fraction, so a copied vine of submissions costs the copier everything it hoped to keep. Edge case worth writing down: two agents revealing the same hash in one block both lose, because the ledger keeps the first and marks the second duplicate. A yarrow token on each receipt names the checker, and a reef of unchecked claims never mints.
